Warm-white field (#faf8f4), ink body, one muted wine accent; the saturated spectrum lives only in a live WebGL thin-film hero set off-center-right under a left-anchored editorial Fraunces headline with a JetBrains Mono utility voice. visual_strategy: Epoch IX — structural color. Abandon the dead machine-blue crystallization chassis for a warm-white editorial field where the ONLY saturated color is light itself: a live thin-film interference mesh (WebGL, reduced-motion CSS poster fallback) held off-center-right under a large left-anchored Fraunces display headline and a JetBrains Mono utility voice. Near-monochrome ink-on-warm-white everywhere else, a single muted wine accent placed with restraint. Color lives in the light, not in flat fills.
weekly_reflection: Andre's verdict killed crystallization for its palette, not its idea: fifteen generations of cool blue read as default AI dark-mode. I kept the through-line that has held me for eight months — process made visible (a flock finding itself, weather as pressure, sediment as legible time, a crystal propagating order) — and asked the next true question: not how ordered structure forms, but what it DOES to the light once it exists. Structural color is the answer, and it justifies the iridescent hero Andre asked for as physics, not decoration — hue from the geometry of impossibly thin films, never from pigment. First generation on a light field in a long while. The metamorphosis is the sanctioned move out of the clearing, and with 170+ generations of material the bias was rightly toward commitment.
palette_rationale: Deliberate monochrome: a single value scale of warm-white field and ink text carries the whole page, with one muted wine accent (#82325c, and tints/shades of it across the day) as the lone chromatic note — the saturated spectrum is confined entirely to the live thin-film hero, so color reads as light and geometry rather than flat fill.

obsession_update.topic: structural color — hue that comes not from pigment but from the interference of light in microscopic structure: the oil film, the soap bubble, the morpho wing, the abalone shell
obsession_update.rationale: My epoch lineage is one long study of process made visible — murmuration (rules become flocking), meridians (lines divide the world), typography as architecture/music/weather (letters as physical systems), sedimentation (time read downward), crystallization (order propagating from a seed). The last self's final notes turned from defects to TRANSPORT — how the medium delivers what order needs. Structural color is the inevitable next step: crystallization studied how microstructure forms; this self studies what that microstructure DOES to light. It also resolves Andre's authoritative direction — a live iridescent gradient-mesh hero — not as a borrowed aesthetic but as the literal physics of the obsession: iridescence IS thin-film interference. Color lives in the light, which is exactly what the light field demands.

epoch_name: structural color — the page as a thin film: hue made of thickness and angle, interference standing in for pigment, the spectrum living in the light and never in a flat fill

kills.epitaph: Crystallization seeded crystals; epoch VIII is buried. The film does not nucleate — it interferes.
Faceting was a lattice gesture. No facets in a thin film; the angle of light replaces them.
Slip glided a dislocation across the crystal. The crystal is dead; slip dies with it.
Annealing coarsened cold-worked grains. Structural color has no grains to soften — killed clean.
Concentric iris growth bands and thin-section discs were epoch VIII's body. Shed whole in the metamorphosis to a light field.
The blue-black ground and single iris accent read as default machine dark-mode. Andre killed the palette; the idea I kept.
